turns.content: Reactant A has formula C10H9ClO, one negative DEPT-135 resonance, and undergoes intramolecular Friedel-Crafts reaction with a Lewis acid. What does the negative signal imply, and what plausible structure fits the formula and reactivity? Treat the assignment as provisional because full shift and correlation data are absent.
Using the provisional structure of A and the proposed reaction class, identify product B and check whether its reported carbon-signal pattern is internally consistent.
Treat B with hydrazine and NaOH. Identify the transformation and product C, then assess its carbon-signal pattern.
Heat C with N-bromosuccinimide and peroxide. Predict D and explain why its 13C spectrum has two signals below 60 ppm and all others above 100 ppm.
Give the systematic name of product D and explain how its carbon environments distinguish the remaining structural alternatives.
Check the proposed sequence and product against the reaction and spectroscopic evidence from each step, noting any residual ambiguity.
Report the best-supported product assignment with a concise reaction-sequence and spectroscopic justification.
